title: refactor(ci): consolidate GitHub Actions workflows, upgrade Node.js to 18, and refresh build deps
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our GitHub Actions surface has drifted into a set of duplicated workflows and brittle cache keys. This PR consolidates CI workflows into a smaller set of composite workflows, upgrades build/test runners to Node.js 18, refreshes caching logic (stable keys + content hashing), and updates a few build/test dev-dependencies. The goal is to reduce maintenance overhead, speed up CI for common paths, and lay the groundwork for future Node 20 upgrades.

What this PR does (high level):
- Consolidates duplicate job definitions into .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/lint.yml using composite actions in .github/actions/ for shared steps.
- Moves all JavaScript/TypeScript jobs to Node.js 18 (setup-node@v4 with cache: 'pnpm') and standardizes npm client to pnpm across CI.
- Replaces several ad-hoc cache keys with a stable cache strategy: OS + node-version + pnpm-lockfile-hash + package-json-hash.
- Updates release automation: migrate release-drafter config to use redwood-release action that supports monorepo changelogs and commit-conventional enforcement.
- Removes deprecated workflows (ci-legacy.yml, ci-node16.yml) and small repo-hygiene fixes (remove old Docker hub push job, bump action versions).
- Bumps a few dev deps that caused CI flakiness: eslint@9.15.0, jest@29.5.0, ts-jest@29.1.0; updated lockfile.

Checklist: 
- [x] Consolidate duplicated steps into composite actions
- [x] Upgrade CI Node version to 18 (all JS jobs)
- [x] Implement stable cache keys and migration notes
- [x] Update release automation and tests for changelog generation
- [x] Run full CI (lint, unit, integration) and fix failures
- [x] Audit and remove deprecated workflows

Testing notes: Ran full CI on branch with matrix=ubuntu-22.04,node18 and a follow-up run for macOS for SDK jobs. Integration tests ran in a reduced matrix to preserve runners; full integration matrix is scheduled on release branches. Local verification performed: pnpm install/build/test on Mac (M1) and Ubuntu container.

Related: ENG-5142 (CI consolidation epic), ENG-5199 (upgrade Node in infra). See internal docs: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5142/ci-consolidation and GH actions docs referenced in the composite actions.

Notes on breaking changes: No runtime or public API changes. CI-only changes. Developers using older local Node versions (<=16) may need to install Node 18 for exact parity with CI; added a note in CONTRIBUTING.md.
commits: ci: upgrade setup-node to v4 and switch default node-version to 18
chore: remove ci-node16.yml and legacy ci workflows
build: refresh pnpm-lock.yaml after bumping eslint/jest/ts-jest
ci(release): switch to redwood-release action and update draft config
review_comments: Jared Bloom: Can we keep a short compatibility window for Node16 images in our Dockerfiles? Some customers still pin. (requested change)
Asha Patel: Answered — kept Docker runtime images at 16 for published runtime images; CI builders use Node18. Added note in Dockerfile and CONTRIBUTING.md.
Maya Chen: Lint job failed on the first run due to cached eslint binary mismatch; recommend invalidating caches when lockfile hash changes. (comment)
Asha Patel: Implemented cache key change to include pnpm-lock.yaml hash and added migration note in docs. Reran CI and tests pass.
Luis Ortega: Approving — good consolidation and caching strategy. Verified release workflow generates changelog as expected. (approved)
ci_checks: Initial run: lint failed (eslint binary mismatch) — cache collision with old key
Fix commit: include lockfile hash in cache key and bump eslint; reran CI
Second run: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration reduced matrix) — full integration scheduled on release branch
Security scan: Snyk scan ran with no new critical findings for updated dev deps
release_notes: CI/refactor: Consolidate workflows, upgrade CI Node to 18, standardize pnpm caching, and refresh dev dependencies (eslint, jest). No runtime API changes. Developers should use Node 18 for CI parity; see CONTRIBUTING.md for notes.
notes: This PR reduces duplicated workflow churn and decreases average CI time for common pull requests by ~22% (observed in pilot runs). Follow-up: schedule Node 20 pilot for non-blocking jobs and migrate remaining images when safe.
